name: Oholibamah
title: Esau's wife from the Hittites
summary: Oholibamah was one of Esau's wives, the daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite. She is mentioned in Genesis as the mother of three of Esau's sons and became a matriarch for several Edomite clans. Her marriage to Esau was part of his connection to the peoples in the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Esau's Marriage to Oholibamah
keyEvents.description: Esau took Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, son of Zibeon the Hivite, as his wife. This was one of several marriages Esau entered into with women from the local peoples.

keyEvents.title: Oholibamah's Sons
keyEvents.description: Oholibamah bore three sons to Esau: Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These became the ancestors of Edomite clans.

keyEvents.title: Moving to the Mountains of Seir
keyEvents.description: Esau took his wives, including Oholibamah, his sons, daughters and all his household, and moved to the mountains of Seir, away from his brother Jacob, because the land could not support them both.

keyEvents.title: Oholibamah's Sons as Chiefs in Edom
keyEvents.description: The sons of Oholibamah—Jeush, Jalam and Korah—became tribal chiefs in the land of Edom. They are specifically mentioned as the sons of Oholibamah, Esau's wife.

keyEvents.title: Oholibamah's Clans in the List of Chiefs
keyEvents.description: In the list of Esau's chiefs, chief Jeush, chief Jalam and chief Korah are mentioned as the clans of Oholibamah's sons in the land of Edom.
